evidence: 10,200 rows for 10,000 unique CustomerIDs; 195 ID groups byte-identical

issue: Conflicting duplicate records (same ID, different SignupDate)
evidence: IDs CUST_248, CUST_308, CUST_333, CUST_391, CUST_466 each appear twice with every other field identical and only SignupDate differing - and in all 5 cases the two dates are an exact month/day swap (CUST_248: 2022-06-09 vs 2022-09-06; CUST_308: 2018-01-03 vs 2018-03-01; CUST_333: 2023-02-11 vs 2023-11-02; CUST_391: 2023-03-11 vs 2023-11-03; CUST_466: 2021-03-07 vs 2021-07-03), i.e. a DD/MM vs MM/DD parsing ambiguity. Neither value in each pair can be trusted, and the same ambiguity may affect records that no duplicate happens to expose
rule: Keep first occurrence, set dq_dup_conflict flag, exclude from modelling

evidence: Exactly 3,500/10,000 = 35.0000% missing; missing rate is flat across Gender (0.341-0.359), Region (0.347-0.353), ContractType (0.346-0.354) and Churn (0.350/0.356) - all inside 3*SE sampling noise
rule: Do not drop rows. Provide Age_imputed (median = 43) behind an explicit flag column

issue: Values from a distinct contaminant distribution (implausible spend)
evidence: 2-component Gaussian mixture separates a component with weight 0.0050 (mean 257, sd 65); BIC improves 89,798 -> 83,646 (dBIC=6,152). A log-normal fitted to the clean body predicts 0.79 rows above 200 but 38 are observed. Highest value 390.30 = 7.8x the median
rule: Set MonthlyCharges_clean = NULL and flag via dq_charge_contaminated
Set MonthlyCharges_clean = NULL and flag via dq_charge_negative

issue: Implausibly low positive charges (below the clean-body minimum)
evidence: Range 0.38-8.74 against a clean-body minimum of 8.89 - too small for any tariff in this product set
rule: Flag via dq_charge_implausible_low for review (not auto-nulled)

issue: Usage rows dated before the customer's signup date
evidence: 2,278 rows (1.90%) across 751 customers; median 48 days and up to 276 days before signup. 751 of the 920 customers who signed up in 2023 received activity from Jan 2023 - the dataset hands every customer a full 12-month 2023 history regardless of when they joined
rule: Cannot be repaired without the source of truth. Flag via dq_pre_signup; exclude pre-signup rows when computing tenure-based metrics

issue: Point mass at exactly 0 GB while call/SMS activity is normal (left-censoring at a floor, not genuine zero usage)
evidence: A smooth Normal(9.90, 3.07) predicts ~0 rows exactly at zero; 58 are observed with none below. Those rows average 518.6 call-minutes vs 492.4 overall, so the customers were clearly active
rule: Flag via dq_data_zero_censored; treat as censored in any average

issue: Distribution is exactly Uniform(0,49) - carries no behavioural structure
evidence: mean 24.525 vs uniform 24.500; sd 14.424 vs uniform 14.430; kurtosis -1.200 vs uniform -1.200; value counts flat (2,297-2,508 per value) with a hard stop at 49. Real SMS behaviour is right-skewed with a mode near zero
rule: Not repairable - record as a data-realism limitation

issue: Behavioural metrics are Gaussian synthetic draws, not real usage shapes
evidence: Kurtosis 0.189 (CallMinutes) and -0.102 (DataUsageGB) against 0.000 for a Normal. Real call and data usage are strongly right-skewed; these are symmetric
rule: Not repairable - record as a data-realism limitation

issue: The churn label has no detectable relationship with any provided feature - the dataset cannot support a predictive churn model
evidence: 5-fold CV ROC-AUC 0.5176 (logistic), 0.5170 (random forest, 500 trees), 0.5164 (gradient boosting) against a 0.5000 random baseline. Shuffling the labels 20 times produced null AUCs up to 0.5372, i.e. the real models score inside the noise band. Single-feature tests: all p>0.11 except SMSCount (p=0.026), which is 1 of 10 tests and therefore expected by chance
rule: Do not sell or build a predictive model on this data; report the label as an uninformative target and treat the exercise as coverage/quality only
